- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in responding to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative after a peak, delay correction by 1–2 days; if sentiment turns positive after a trough, anticipate 1–2 day lag in price rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce noise in forecast tails.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day average to avoid overestimation.
